provenance_note: The reference corpus was authored independently without access to the tool code; this run recomputes every check from the shipping build.
reference: Scenario corpus of bow-tie models built from spec 03 (MVP scope, rules, acceptance criteria), spec 00-common (insufficient data, stable ids, explicit negative handling) and public barrier-management guidance: the CCPS-EI bow-tie pitfalls paper (Johnson, Manton, Cowley, Scanlon, Hazards 28, 2018: effective/independent/auditable, detect-decide-act, prevention left / mitigation right, degradation factors and controls, barrier count per pathway) and PSA Norway barrier-management principles (2013: verifiable performance requirements, verification, independence). Covers complete models, the function+criterion+verification adequacy test, evidence/owner/frequency, side placement, detection without action, common-cause sharing of each element category and upstream dependency, count versus independence, graph integrity, degradation controls, insufficient data, rename/reorder/round-trip id stability, import refusals, and 10 randomized models (10/30/80 barriers among them, seed 20260916) whose counts come from ref.py. Inputs are tool-neutral: 'key' values are local handles that the harness maps to the tool's UUIDs; empty string or null means the field is left blank; shared_elements not listed as shared carry unique identifiers.
reference_citations: M. Johnson, M. Manton, C. Cowley, M. Scanlon, 'Bow Ties in Risk Management; using the new CCPS-EI book to avoid pitfalls', IChemE Symposium Series No 163, Hazards 28, 2018, https://www.icheme.org/media/16937/hazards-28-paper-31.pdf (pp. 2-5)

Petroleum Safety Authority Norway, Principles for barrier management in the petroleum industry, 29.01.2013, https://www.havtil.no/contentassets/11851dc03a84473e8299a2d80e656356/principles-for-barrier-management-in-the-petroleum-industry_2013.pdf (Definitions p.3; p.13; p.26)

IOGP Report 544, Standardization of barrier definitions (supplement to Report 415), April 2016, https://www.iogp.org/bookstore/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/woocommerce_uploads/2016/10/544.pdf (p.9 barrier definition; context only)
tools.petrov.re spec 03 Bow-Tie Builder (MVP scope, model rules, results, acceptance criteria) and spec 00-common sections 0.4, 0.5, Appendices B and C
tolerance: All checks exact: counts are integers, statuses and finding presence are categorical, and the tool performs no numerical computation (the spec forbids probability reduction), so no tolerance other than identity is meaningful. Rule ids in check names (BT-R-0xx) are README labels to help the harness locate the finding; the expectation is the semantic finding named before them, grounded in the cited basis. '_positive' checks mean the value is > 0; '_is_complete: false' checks accept any non-complete status.

not_benchmarked.Identifier normalisation: Case/whitespace normalisation of shared-element identifiers (README behaviour; no source defines it).
not_benchmarked.Multi-category flag count: Exact dependency_flags count when a pair shares several categories (tool convention).
not_benchmarked.Nameless items and cross-pathway depende: Nameless items (BT-R-018) and dependency on a barrier of another pathway (BT-R-014 variant): no source or spec criterion fixes the expected outcome.
not_benchmarked.Report and interface qualities: PDF readability on A4 landscape, clickable findings, visual QA of 10/30/80-barrier figures, keyboard and mobile register view: UI/visual, not expressible as reference values.
not_benchmarked.Paywalled standards: IEC 61511 / IEC 61508 independence clauses and ISO 31000: not read (paywalled); used only as named conceptual basis via the spec, never as a limit.
not_benchmarked.CCPS/EI book: CCPS/EI book (2018) itself was not read; its content is used only as summarised in the Hazards 28 paper by its authors.
not_benchmarked.Exchange document: safety-exchange bowtie.barriers document shape and incidenttree handoff.

harness.note: bash harness/qa.sh bowtiebuilder.html 8203: manifest, catalog, seven-language UI at 390 and 1280 px, report PDFs in seven languages, domain self-tests, artifact regeneration and benchmark page.

domain_self_tests.note: window.__safetyTests(): rule-by-rule, boundary, negative, insufficient-data, round-trip, import and figure cases.

reference_mapping.note: Reference keys map to deterministic UUIDs; shared_elements map to power/sensor/operator/procedure; controls are joined into the degradation control text.

coverage.note: Spec 03 MVP: barrier types, barrier fields, degradation factor + control, common-cause by power supply/sensor/operator/procedure/upstream barrier, register counts (threat_count, consequence_count, preventive_barriers, mitigative_barriers, incomplete_barriers, dependency_flags). Rules: adequacy test, side placement, detection-without-action, count vs quality/independence, no probability reduction, no automatic acceptability. QA: graph integrity, stable UUIDs, rename stability, incomplete and dependency rule tests, 10/30/80-barrier models (counts only). Spec 00: insufficient data and explicit negative imports.
